chinese_source: Dirghagama (T.1), sutra 27 (Shamenguo jing), read out by Buddhayasas, translated by Zhu Fonian, Chang'an; second recension in Yijing's Mulasarvavastivada Vinaya Sanghabhedavastu (T.1450), 710
date_raw: Later Qin, Hongshi era (translation completed 413 CE)
event: The six sramana teachers - Purana Kassapa, Makkhali Gosala, Ajita Kesakambala, Pakudha Kaccayana, Sanjaya Belatthiputta, Nigantha Nataputta (Mahavira) - are preserved as a fixed list with fixed one-line doctrines in the Sramanyaphala-sutra as translated into Chinese in 413 CE: a TAQ for the six-teachers stratum as fossilised syllabus material
firmness_reason: The Dirghagama translation date (412-413) is catalogue/colophon record; the bound applies to the textual stratum, not to the teachers' floruits, which rest on the Buddha-synchronism of tradition class
indian_entity: The six sramana teachers (Purana, Gosala, Ajita, Pakudha, Sanjaya, Nigantha Nataputta)
notes: Campaign 2 case E2: carried so the tool records the distinction this campaign insists on - China dates the list, not the men. Mahavira's own interval is chained to the Buddha result (MAHAVIRA.md E1), not derived from this record.

chinese_source: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji (Pundravardhana and Samatata chapters; India taxonomy juan 2); record presented 646
event: Xuanzang counts the naked Nirgranthas (Jains) as the most numerous non-Buddhist sectaries at Pundravardhana and again at Samatata, and describes the order from observation (naked, hair-plucking, cracked skin) - a dated eyewitness snapshot of Jain communities thriving across Bengal eleven centuries after Mahavira
firmness_reason: Dated eyewitness observation, the spine's zero-lag class; graded probable because the pilgrim's 'most numerous' is an impression, not a census, and the Ni-kien = Nirgrantha = Jain identification, though standard, is an identification
notes: Campaign 2 case E3: pins the order's survival and distribution in the 7th century; says nothing about its origins. No anchor is offered for Mahavira himself, Parsva, Gosala or the Buddha's teachers - the Chinese record dates none of them (MAHAVIRA.md E1, E4-E6).
references: Da Tang Xiyu Ji, Pundravardhana / Samatata chapters
Beal, Si-yu-ki (Buddhist Records of the Western World)
